note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following stable ISUP grade group 2 findings on repeat biopsy.

Recently retired civil servant presenting for urological re-evaluation. He has a known history of prostate cancer diagnosed on biopsy, with stable ISUP grade group 2 findings. Medical history includes type 2 diabetes managed with metformin and hypercholesterolaemia treated with atorvastatin and simvastatin. He reports no significant lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 0. Socially, he is married, lives in a ground-floor apartment with his partner, and cycles approximately 20 km twice weekly. He is an ex-smoker who quit in 2004. Recent dental check-ups have been unremarkable. He notes visual impairment requiring large-print correspondence.

Per rectum, a distinct nodule is palpable in the left lobe of the prostate, consistent with clinical stage cT2. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.

living: Lives in ground-floor apartment with partner
